evidence.title: The AI Roadmap: How We Ensure AI Serves Humanity
evidence.what: CHT's seven-principle policy roadmap; Principle 7 says a few firms 'hoard development resources' and calls for a more balanced distribution of AI power.

evidence.title: Litigation case study: Character.AI and Google (Garcia v. Character Technologies)
evidence.what: CHT is expert consultant to plaintiff counsel, arguing the race to AGI drove unsafe engagement-maximizing companion design; frames AI companies as unaccountable.

evidence.title: Control Your Tech Use (take-control guide) and Foundations of Humane Technology course
evidence.what: CHT's public guide explicitly recommends 'adding friction' (hide apps, pause tools) against notification/engagement design; its free course trains builders in humane, non-extractive design.

evidence.title: Talk, Trust, and Trade-Offs: How and Why Teens Use AI Companions
evidence.what: National survey (July 2025): 72% of teens have used AI companions; CSM recommends no one under 18 use them and backs legislation banning them for minors.

evidence.title: Research brief: Teens, Trust, and Technology in the Age of AI
evidence.what: Survey of 1,045 teens: 64% say tech companies can't be trusted to care about their well-being; 73% want AI-generated content labeled; 70% want AI privacy safeguards.

evidence.title: Protecting Kids Online in the AI Era: The Path Forward
evidence.what: 2026 policy paper arguing notice-and-consent is inadequate for AI, calling for data minimization, bans on training on kids' inputs, and COPPA updates.

evidence.title: Amicus brief in Musk v. Altman / 'Not For Private Gain' campaign
evidence.what: Encode filed to block OpenAI's for-profit conversion and co-led a coalition to keep nonprofit control, framing a few companies internalizing profits while externalizing risk.

evidence.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act / DEFIANCE Act coalition and petition on non-consensual deepfakes
evidence.what: Encode and ARI ran a petition and coalition letter that helped pass a federal law criminalizing non-consensual AI deepfake imagery - consent harm from AI, not agents.

evidence.title: State AI safety laws: California SB 53, New York RAISE Act, Illinois SB 315
evidence.what: Encode lists these frontier-model transparency/audit laws as wins; they are concrete legislation, though oriented to frontier/catastrophic risk more than everyday harms.

evidence.title: Our Priorities - 'Current Harms' track
evidence.what: ARI's priorities explicitly include present-day harms (chatbot impersonation disclosure, labor-market data, creator opt-outs, deepfakes, election deception) alongside emerging risks.

evidence.title: Endorsement of the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act (non-personified default)
evidence.what: ARI proposed and then endorsed a bipartisan bill requiring chatbots to default to non-human personas for minors - a concrete, everyday-harm AI safety measure.

evidence.title: President Signs the TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what: ARI co-ran the Encode/ARI deepfake petition campaign that preceded the federal non-consensual deepfake law.

evidence.title: Impact page: California Age-Appropriate Design Code (2022), Maryland and Vermont Kids Codes, KOSA/COPPA 2.0 Senate passage (2024)
evidence.what: Youth coalition that grew out of the CA AADC campaign; led passage of state design-code laws and lobbied for KOSA, framed as 'user wellbeing over Big Tech's profit'.

evidence.title: Design It For Us Applauds Governor Newsom for Signing Landmark Design-Feature Legislation
evidence.what: Press release on California design-feature (addictive feeds) law the coalition backed, a concrete youth well-being policy win.

evidence.what: Grants in three areas including $360K for youth peer-to-peer support programs (Big Brothers Big Sisters CO, Colorado Youth Congress, The Center on Colfax) plus a grantee Community of Practice.

evidence.what: Funder collaborative's first grants to Think:Kids/Meadows MHPI ($2M), The Path Forward ($1.8M) and The Jed Foundation ($1.5M).

evidence.what: Report (with Morgan Stanley Children's Mental Health Alliance) surveying funders on barriers to youth mental health giving and proposing five solutions.

evidence.what: Fund launched 2019 giving $100K unrestricted grants plus capacity support to nonpartisan organizations rebuilding civic trust (e.g., BLOC, Liberation Ventures, Rise).

evidence.what: Sehra, now CEO, led New Profit's education portfolio for 14 years and the $38M Reimagine Learning fund backing 25 organizations.

evidence.title: $220M+ in K-8 literacy and math grants
evidence.what: Active grant portfolio including Accelerate's State Implementation Fund, Renaissance Philanthropy's LEVI Literacy, and Modern Classrooms coaching for 4,000 math teachers.

evidence.title: $20M for career-connected learning
evidence.what: Grants to CityWorks, EmployIndy, New America's Partnership to Advance Youth Apprenticeship, Catalyze Challenge and Urban Alliance under Strategy 2025.

evidence.title: K-12 math strategy (10-year cornerstone)
evidence.what: Fact sheet making math the center of Gates' K-12 strategy: instructional materials, teacher prep, district systems, HS-to-college pathways; builds on Balance the Equation and Networks for School Improvement.
